title: The Vikings
examples: How did the Vikings travel so far away?
Were the Vikings always fighting people?

explain.say: The Vikings were people who came from Scandinavia. They were from areas like modern-day Denmark, Norway, and Sweden.
They built amazing boats called longships. These ships were fast and could travel on rivers and the open sea.
The Vikings were known for being raiders. Sometimes they attacked monasteries or towns to take goods.
But they were also skilled traders. They traded things like furs, slaves, and valuable metals for other goods.
Eventually, they stayed in new lands. They built permanent settlements in places like Ireland and parts of England.
A real-life example is when people today move to a new country. They build new homes and start trading with the local people.

faq.q: Did all Vikings live on longships?
faq.a: No, they used longships for travel, but once they settled, they built more permanent buildings.

faq.q: Did they only raid Christian places?
faq.a: No, they traded with many different groups of people across various cultures.

faq.q: What was the most important thing they traded?
faq.a: They traded many things, but metals and valuable goods like furs were very important to them.

faq.q: Did they always fight people they met?
faq.a: Not always. They were skilled traders and sometimes they were welcomed into new communities.

faq.q: Where did they settle after raiding?
faq.a: They settled in many places, including parts of England and Ireland, creating new communities.

facts: Longships were designed to be fast on both rivers and open seas.
The Vikings were known for both raiding and establishing trade networks.
They settled in various regions, including parts of modern-day England and Ireland.
They traded goods such as furs, slaves, and valuable metals.

quiz.say: The Vikings were primarily from which region?
quiz.why: Scandinavia is the area that includes Denmark, Norway, and Sweden, which is where the Vikings originated.

wrong.1: Britain was where they traveled to raid and settle, but it was not their home area.
wrong.2: Germany was a place they traded with, but it was not their primary homeland.
wrong.3: Italy was not a known origin point for the Viking people.

quiz.say: What was the main purpose of the longship?

options.show: To travel on both rivers and seas
options.say: To travel on both rivers and seas

quiz.why: The longship's design allowed it to navigate different types of water bodies effectively.

wrong.0: Their design prioritized speed and maneuverability over massive cargo loads.
wrong.1: They also used them extensively for peaceful trade.
wrong.3: They needed to travel up rivers to reach inland settlements.

quiz.say: When Vikings settled, what did they do besides building homes?
quiz.why: Settlements were not just about living; they were also centers for exchanging goods.

wrong.1: Raiding was only one part of their activities; trade was also important.
wrong.2: Archaeologists have found many signs of their trading activities.
wrong.3: While they farmed, their economic activity was much broader than just agriculture.
